compatibilityResearch.question: Whether OWL2VOWL creates a VOWL entity for a property that is declared but carries no property axioms
compatibilityResearch.publicBasis: VOWL 2.0 specification and the pinned OWL2VOWL 0.3.7 reference outputs under src/owl2vowl/test/fixtures/java-reference-outputs/
compatibilityResearch.reason: A corpus difference showed 95 declaration-only properties emitted by VOWLBuilder and absent from the reference output. The output alone could not distinguish between several candidate causes, so the converter's orchestration was read to establish how its entity set is formed.
compatibilityResearch.finding: Entities are established in preParsing by an OWLOntologyWalker driving an EntityCreationVisitor across the whole imports closure, before any axiom-driven phase runs. The later per-property axiom loops decorate entities that already exist; they do not create them. A declared property therefore does appear, which the phase5-structural reference output confirms for a property carrying nothing but a declaration.
compatibilityResearch.productionUse: None. A filter written on the mistaken reading that axioms create entities was reverted in full before any commit, together with the test that encoded it. No implementation text or control flow was copied.

compatibilityResearch.question: What the VOWL-JSON `instances` count on a class actually counts, given that it disagrees with the length of the same entry's `individuals` array
compatibilityResearch.publicBasis: VOWL 2.0 specification and the pinned OWL2VOWL 0.3.7 reference outputs under src/owl2vowl/test/fixtures/java-reference-outputs/
compatibilityResearch.reason: The reference outputs establish that the two fields are independent - only 6 of 9102 class entries carry a non-zero `instances`, and `time-gregorian.ttl` renders `MonthOfYear` with `instances: 1` beside eleven `individuals` - but they cannot reveal the rule that separates them. VOWL 2.0 does not specify the serialisation, so neither source of evidence could settle it.
compatibilityResearch.finding: `IndividualsVisitor` branches on whether the individual's IRI is also present in the class map. When it is, the IRI is recorded as an instance; otherwise it is recorded as an individual. `instances` therefore counts class-and-individual punning, which OWL 2 permits, and never the ordinary members of a class. That is why it is almost always zero and why it is unrelated to the length of `individuals`.
compatibilityResearch.productionUse: None. No implementation text or control flow was copied; the rule was reimplemented independently in VOWLBuilder against project-owned tests.

compatibilityResearch.question: Whether OWL2VOWL restricts entities drawn from imported ontologies to those the importing document references
compatibilityResearch.publicBasis: VOWL 2.0 specification and the pinned OWL2VOWL 0.3.7 reference outputs
compatibilityResearch.reason: tagont.owl produced 77 more properties than the reference output, all of them from imported namespaces rather than declared in the document.
compatibilityResearch.finding: No such restriction exists. The reference output emits 20 skos/core entities that tagont.owl never mentions and 99 such entities for dcat3.rdf, so imports were resolved and imported entities were not filtered by reference. The difference is instead an asymmetry of inputs: tagont.owl imports the long-dead http://www.mindswap.org/2003/owl/foaf, which the reference run could not fetch, while the project's ONTOLOGY_CATALOG maps that IRI to a local FOAF copy. The two sides converted different ontologies.
compatibilityResearch.productionUse: None. The finding is a property of the differential harness rather than of either engine, and no production behavior was changed.
